newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - heavy fuel continues to buck tren.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - heavy fuel continues to buck tren.

text.p: European oil swaps were steady on Thursday, apart from heavy fuel oil which gained $1-2 a tonne. Traders said tightness in the physical fuel market was the main support.
Heavy fuel swaps rose by a touch under $2 a tonne with June pegged around $86.50 and July around $87.
Dealers said the push came from the physical market where barges traded at $86.50 and $87.

Fuel has been bucking the general trend in recent days -- not following crude -- and traders said today's movement was an extension of this. Low sulphur swaps were steady around $92.50 for June although there was talk at higher levels earlier.
Gasoline swaps were also unchanged around $203 for June with July backwardated $6 or so. A physical eurograde barge sold at $202 fob which dealers thought was a touch below the market.
Naphtha swaps were steady, but slow. Nothing was heard on June, but July was thought to have traded at $185, unchanged from Wednesday.
Brent crude CFDs were essentially static with June 9-13 pegged around -41/42 cents under July Brent and June 16-20 at -34/35 under. No CFDs were heard sold.
The gas oil 4Q crack spread widened a touch to $4.80 from the $4.75 seen trading yesterday while 1Q98 broaded to $4.70 from $4.60.
